battle.name: 赫蒙杜里-查蒂戰爭
battle.theater: 易北河上游與韋拉河谷地
battle.brief: 公元58年前後，查蒂人與赫蒙杜里人在易北河上游與黑森高地之間打了一場沒有決戰的邊境消耗戰，唯一出處是塔西佗《日耳曼尼亞》第四十三章。卡面的埃及月牙劍是前1500年前後的青銅柴刀，較本役早了三個半千年，它是對照件：本役真正在場的是日耳曼部族的鐵短劍、木盾與短矛。

kit.name: 埃及月牙劍
kit.history: 外彎的單刃劍，砍下去不用拔。它比直劍更早出現在埃及人的手上。

countries: 這場赫蒙杜里－查蒂戰爭，是公元一世紀中葉日耳曼世界內部一場沒有大戰的邊境戰，交戰雙方都沒有留下自己的記載，唯一提到它的是塔西佗《日耳曼尼亞》第四十三章。查蒂人住在易北河上游以西的陶努斯森林與威悉河上游之間，是中日耳曼最大的部族聯盟之一：沒有王，沒有常備軍，戰力靠各部族首領臨時徵召的步兵，戰與和由固定的集會場所決定；他們以嚴整的圍城紀律與把誓言按在劍上的風俗聞名，羅馬人要等到圖拉真與圖密善時代才正式把他們當成前線上的對手與對象。赫蒙杜里人住在易北河中下游兩岸，今薩克森－安哈特一帶，向上伸到薩勒河與翁施特魯特河；他們在河谷裡控制東西通道，據後世喬達尼斯在《哥特人史》的說法，早期汪達爾人一度被稱為「赫蒙杜里」，所以不少學者視兩者為同一族群的先後名字。第三方是羅馬：公元58年前後，萊茵邊界與上日耳曼前線正沿陶努斯、韋拉河與易北河上游向北推進，赫蒙杜里人既被徵為輔助兵，又夾在羅馬與查蒂人之間，是這場戰爭真正的壓力來源。整場衝突沒有陣亡數字、沒有俘虜數、沒有戰利品記錄，只剩下攻守的回合與地理。
countriesEn: The Hermunduri–Chatti war was a border war without a battle, fought inside the Germanic world in the middle of the first century AD. Neither side left an account of it, and the only mention of it comes from Tacitus, Germania, chapter 43. The Chatti occupied the country between the Taunus forest and the upper Weser, west of the upper Elbe, and were one of the largest tribal confederations of central Germany: no king, no standing army, the fighting strength being infantry levied on the spot by clan leaders, with war and peace decided in fixed assembly places. They were known for their disciplined siege work and for the custom of swearing oaths on the blade of the sword, and only under Trajan and Domitian did the Romans come to treat them openly as a frontier opponent and then as a client. The Hermunduri lived on the middle and lower Elbe, in what is now Saxony-Anhalt, reaching up the Saale and the Unstrut; they controlled the east–west passages of the river valleys, and according to Jordanes in the Getica the early Vandals were once called Hermunduri, so many scholars treat the two names as successive forms of one people. The third party was Rome: around AD 58 the Rhine frontier and the Upper German military line were pushing north along the Taunus, the Werra and the upper Elbe, and the Hermunduri were both recruited as auxiliaries and wedged between Rome and the Chatti, which was the real source of pressure in this war. The whole conflict left no figures for dead, prisoners or booty; only the alternation of attack and counter-attack, and the geography, survive.
people: 這場戰爭沒有留下任何一個將領的名字，這本身就是它最該被記住的事實。查蒂人由各部族首領率領，沒有留下戰爭統帥的記載；赫蒙杜里人同樣沒有留下名號。唯一能為這場戰爭作證的關鍵人物是普布利烏斯·科爾涅利烏斯·塔西佗（約公元55年至120年）：他是元老院議員，公元97年出任執政官，一般認為曾任下日耳曼與亞細亞的行省總督，長期研究日耳曼問題，《日耳曼尼亞》約在公元98年成書，全書四十六章，第四十三章記錄查蒂人，第四十五章前後描述易北河下游的居民，這就是這場戰爭唯一的文字出處。塔西佗並不是為戰爭寫作，而是在寫一部民族志；正因如此，他給出的是結構而不是場面：地理、習俗、戰法、交戰的歷史。與這場戰爭有間接關係的，還有幾位後世人物。公元69年至70年的巴達維亞起義中，易北河下游的赫蒙杜里人作為羅馬盟軍出現在戰線上，說明這場邊境戰爭的直接後果，是羅馬在前線多了一批必須維持住的盟友。公元75年至76年圖密善對查蒂人與馬提亞基人的戰役，把查蒂人從戰爭的一方變成羅馬必須直接處置的對象。公元六世紀的喬達尼斯在《哥特人史》裡把汪達爾人的古名指回「赫蒙杜里」，讓這場公元58年前後的戰爭，成為後世追溯族群遷徙時一個很早的錨點。
peopleEn: Not a single commander of this war has left a name, and that is itself the fact most worth recording. The Chatti were led by clan chiefs, with no recorded war commander, and the Hermunduri left no names either. The one key figure who can testify to this war is Publius Cornelius Tacitus (c. AD 55–120): a senator, consul in AD 97, generally held to have governed Lower Germany and later Asia, and a long-time student of Germanic affairs. His Germania was completed around AD 98 and runs to forty-six chapters; chapter 43 describes the Chatti, and the passage around chapter 45 describes the people of the lower Elbe, and these are the only written traces of the war. Tacitus was not writing a history of a war: he was writing an ethnographic survey, which is exactly why what he gives is structure rather than scene — country, custom, method of fighting, the record of a contest. Indirectly connected to the war are several later figures. In the Batavian revolt of AD 69–70 the Hermunduri of the lower Elbe appear on the war line as allies of Rome, which shows that the direct consequence of this border war was one more set of allies Rome had to keep in being. The campaigns of Domitian against the Chatti and the Mattiaci in AD 75–76 turned the Chatti from one party in a tribal war into a problem Rome had to settle directly. And in AD 551 Jordanes, in the Getica, pointed the ancient name of the Vandals back to 'Hermunduri', making this war of around AD 58 an early anchor for later accounts of migration.
kits: 卡面是埃及月牙劍（Khopesh）：一柄外彎、單刃、刃口朝內的青銅柴刀，形制可上溯到前王朝晚期的斧形武器，新王國時期約前1500年定型為軍用刀身，砍下去不必拔刀，傷口靠勾拉撕開。它在本役的位置是對照件，不是戰場所用：本役發生在公元一世紀中葉，比這件兵器晚了三千五百年上下，新王國之後的埃及已改用直身銅劍與後來的鐵劍，月牙劍本身在羅馬時代早已是古物。真正在場的日耳曼兵器是鐵的。塔西佗在《日耳曼尼亞》第六與第二十五至二十六章描述的配備是：木框大盾，多為橢圓形或長方形，排列成盾牆；一柄短鐵劍，薩克式的寬厚刀身既能劈砍也能突刺；標槍與短矛，最長的矛在近身戰中用來刺穿盾陣；還有小型弓與短箭，用於騷擾與偵察，而不是密集火力。此外是圍城器材：柴束、泥土填塞、盾陣遮蔽下的接近，以及木柵與壕溝。鐵的供應不是問題，來源在日耳曼山地與礦區，羅馬人自己也說這些部族是以鐵武裝的。至於馬匹，日耳曼騎兵確實存在，但以步兵為榮耀、騎兵只作追擊與偵察之用，這在《日耳曼尼亞》第三與第六章都寫得明白。
kitsEn: The card shows the khopesh: an outward-curving, single-edged bronze cleaver whose cutting edge faces inward, a form that descends from axe-shaped weapons of the late Old Kingdom and was fixed as a military blade in the New Kingdom around 1500 BC, striking downwards so that there was no need to pull the blade back out, the wound being opened by the hook of the curve. Its place in this war is that of a reference piece, not a weapon in the field: the war was fought in the middle of the first century AD, some three and a half millennia after this blade, and Egypt after the New Kingdom had already gone over to straight bronze swords and later iron, so the khopesh was already an antiquity in Roman times. What was actually present was iron. The equipment Tacitus describes in Germania 6 and 25–26 is this: large wooden shields, oval or oblong, set side by side as a shield wall; a short iron sword of the seax type, broad enough to cut and to thrust; spears and javelins, the longest spear used at close quarters to pierce the shield line; and a small bow with short arrows, used to harass and to scout rather than to deliver massed fire. There was also siege equipment: fascines, earth fill, approach under the cover of shields, wooden palisades and ditches. Iron supply was no problem either, the metal coming from the mountains and mining districts of the German uplands; the Romans themselves said these peoples were armed with iron. As for horses, Germanic cavalry did exist, but the glory of Germanic arms lay with the infantry, and cavalry was used for pursuit and scouting, as Germania 3 and 6 make plain.
tactics: 塔西佗筆下沒有這場戰爭的某一場戰鬥，但他給了日耳曼戰法的全貌。步兵不結方陣，而是結成鬆散的楔形或新月形，前排擠壓、後排支撐，靠人數與地形的厚度取勝；開戰前是齊射的標槍與短矛，接近到盾與盾相接的距離才拔劍；大型木盾不只護身，還用來搭盾牆，弓手則在側翼放冷箭，騷擾對方陣腳。日耳曼部族之間的戰爭多不是會戰，而是襲擾與反襲擾：燒村、奪牲口、破壞田地，然後退回林地。這也是為什麼塔西佗特別留意查蒂人攻城的紀律——他們不用臨時衝撞，而是步步為營，用柴束與土石填平壕溝，舉盾遮蔽接近，把攻城變成耐力與工兵的較量。赫蒙杜里人的地利是易北河與其支流的河谷：河道擋住平原上的正面推進，渡口與淺灘是唯一可以讓隊伍成列通過的地方，退入河曲就能脫離接觸。對查蒂人來說，向東推進要面對的正是這種水系縱橫的地形；而羅馬人設在河谷的驛站與軍鎮，又把整個區域變成可以下達命令的縱深。沒有縱深補給線，沒有統一指揮，戰事因此變成兩族之間不斷互換的攻守：燒掉對方前哨、拉走牲口、趁雨季或冬季越過山脊突襲，再在對方反應過來之前退回森林。
tacticsEn: Tacitus gives no single engagement of this war, but he gives the whole picture of German warfare. The infantry did not form a phalanx: they formed a loose wedge or crescent, the front ranks compressed and the rear supporting them, winning on numbers and on the weight of the ground. The opening was a volley of spears and javelins, and the sword was drawn only once shield met shield. The big wooden shield was not merely protection but also the material of the shield wall, while the archers loosed cold arrows from the flanks to unsettle the enemy's footing. Wars between Germanic peoples were rarely set-piece battles but raids and counter-raids: burning villages, taking cattle, breaking the fields, and then withdrawing into the woods, which is why Tacitus pays particular attention to the discipline of the Chatti in storming towns — they did not charge in improvising, but advanced step by step, filling the ditches with fascines and earth and covering the approach with shields, turning an assault into a trial of patience and engineering. The Hermunduri's advantage of position was the Elbe and the valleys of its tributaries: the river blocked frontal advance across the plain, fords and shallows were the only places a column could cross in line, and a withdrawal into a bend of the river broke contact. For the Chatti, pushing east meant facing precisely that network of waterways, while the Roman stations and forts in the valleys turned the whole region into a depth in which orders could be carried out. With no line of supply and no unified command, the fighting became a constant exchange of blows between the two peoples: burn the enemy's outpost, drive off the cattle, cross the ridge in the wet season or in winter and strike, and be back in the forest before the other side could react.
data: 這場戰爭最特別的地方，是它幾乎沒有數字。塔西佗沒有寫下任何一場戰役的日期、雙方兵力、陣亡與俘虜數，也沒有戰利品清單；他寫的是「查蒂人與赫蒙杜里人交戰」這件事本身，以及戰局的反覆。能夠核對的只有框架：塔西佗《日耳曼尼亞》成書於公元98年上下，全書四十六章，其中第四十三章與第四十五章前後涉及查蒂人與易北河下游的赫蒙杜里人；戰爭本身通常被放在公元一世紀中葉，公元58年前後是一個常用的定位。地理尺度可以估算：查蒂人的核心在陶努斯森林與威悉河上游之間，赫蒙杜里人在易北河中下游的薩勒河與翁施特魯特河一帶，兩地相距以現代公路里程估算大約三百到四百公里，其間夾著的是圖林根與黑森一帶的山地與河谷。這個距離說明，這不是一場可以在同一處解決的戰爭，而是一條綿延的邊境線上的拉鋸。數字缺口的另一面是一個明確的結論：任何把雙方兵力寫成幾萬的說法，都沒有文本依據；能確定的只有交戰雙方的族屬、地理、大致的年代，以及它是一場反覆進行、而非一次決戰的邊境衝突。
dataEn: What is most unusual about this war is that it has almost no figures. Tacitus records no date for any engagement, no strengths, no deaths or prisoners, and no list of booty; what he records is the fact of the war itself, the Chatti fighting with the Hermunduri, and the way the situation kept turning. Only the frame can be checked: the Germania was written around AD 98 and runs to forty-six chapters, of which chapter 43 and the passage around chapter 45 concern the Chatti and the Hermunduri of the lower Elbe; the war itself is usually placed in the middle of the first century AD, and around AD 58 is a common dating. The scale of geography can be estimated: the core of the Chatti lay between the Taunus forest and the upper Weser, the Hermunduri on the middle Elbe around the Saale and the Unstrut, and the two territories lie roughly three hundred to four hundred kilometres apart by modern road distance, with the uplands and river valleys of Thuringia and Hesse in between. That distance shows this was not a war that could be settled in one place, but a tug-of-war along a long border. The other face of the numerical gap is a firm conclusion: any claim that either side fielded tens of thousands has no basis in the text. What is certain is the identity of the belligerents, the geography, the rough date, and the fact that this was a recurring border conflict rather than one decisive battle.
cause: 打起來的原因有三層，而且每一層都不是「誰得罪了誰」這種可以指認的理由。最外層是土地：塔西佗在《日耳曼尼亞》第三與第二十八章解釋日耳曼部族為何年年遷徙——人口稠密而土地不夠，人數一多就被迫往外走，於是形成一條朝東與朝南擠壓的連鎖；公元一世紀中葉，東邊的馬科曼尼、夸迪與各種東日耳曼聯盟同時南移，最前線的推力就落到易北河一帶。中層是位置：赫蒙杜里人卡在查蒂人與羅馬之間，東面擠著南來的部族聯盟，西面是查蒂人的劫掠，南面則是羅馬萊茵邊界的駐軍與軍鎮；羅馬需要有人守住易北河的上游通道，於是把赫蒙杜里人拉進同盟體系，而同盟者之間的邊境掠奪因此變得無法容忍。內層是部族自身的做法：查蒂人以劫掠與圍城維持戰士的回報，以對劍起誓的風俗維持內部團結，掠奪邊境是他們認為正當的生計；赫蒙杜里人則必須靠河谷地勢與羅馬的關係守住自己的牧場與耕地。兩邊都知道對方不會被一次打垮，於是戰爭變成雙方都不能先停手的消耗。
causeEn: There were three layers of cause, and not one of them is a reason of the 'who offended whom' kind that can be pointed at. The outermost was land: in Germania 3 and 28 Tacitus explains why Germanic peoples moved year by year — the population is dense and the land insufficient, so as numbers grow they are driven outward, producing a chain of pressure running east and south. In the middle of the first century AD the Marcomanni, the Quadi and the various eastern Germanic groupings moved south at the same time, and the leading edge of that pressure came to rest on the Elbe. The middle layer was position: the Hermunduri were caught between the Chatti and Rome, pressed from the east by the southern-moving tribal alliances, raided from the west by the Chatti, and on the south by the garrison and forts of the Roman Rhine frontier. Rome needed someone to hold the upper-Elbe corridor, so it drew the Hermunduri into its system of alliance, and border plunder between allies became impossible to tolerate. The innermost layer was the practice of the tribes themselves: the Chatti maintained the returns of their warriors by plunder and by siege, held their people together with the custom of swearing on the sword, and regarded border raiding as legitimate livelihood; the Hermunduri, for their part, had to use the river valleys and their relationship with Rome to hold their pastures and their fields. Both sides knew the other could not be destroyed in one stroke, and so the war became a consumption neither could afford to end first.
impact: 影響分三層。對當時的日耳曼世界，赫蒙杜里－查蒂戰爭把易北河上游變成一條誰也不能放棄的邊界線：赫蒙杜里人被推向羅馬，靠軍鎮與輔助兵身份換取保護，這條依附關係日後讓他們在公元69年至70年的巴達維亞起義中站在羅馬一邊，也讓易北河上游的聚落開始被寫進羅馬的行政與地理文獻。對查蒂人，這場戰爭把他們從一個地方強權推成了羅馬必須正視的前線對手：公元75年至76年圖密善的戰役之後，羅馬在陶努斯與威悉河上游之間修築上日耳曼界牆，設立薩爾堡等軍鎮，把這一帶的走廊地帶收編為羅馬的盟邦與輔助兵來源；查蒂人的名字也就此留在地名裡，今日的「黑森」（Hessen）之名，學界通常認為源自「查蒂人」（Chatti）的族名。對後世的軍事思想，這場戰爭是一次罕見的「無記錄戰爭」樣本：雙方都沒有留下戰報，我們只能從一部民族志裡的一句話重建一整條邊境；它提醒人，多數古代戰爭不是以會戰收場，而是以攻守的耐力與地理的縱深收場。
impactEn: The effects worked on three levels. For the Germanic world of the day, the Hermunduri–Chatti war turned the upper Elbe into a frontier line that nobody could afford to give up: the Hermunduri were pushed west against Rome and exchanged dependence for protection, and that relationship later placed them on the Roman side of the Batavian revolt of AD 69–70, while the settlements of the upper Elbe began to appear in Roman administrative and geographical records. For the Chatti, the war turned them from a regional power into an opponent Rome had to face: after the campaigns of AD 75–76, Domitian built the Upper German limes between the Taunus and the upper Weser, established forts such as Saalburg, and drew the corridor of country there into the Roman system of client states and sources of auxiliary recruits. The name of the Chatti was thus preserved in place-names: modern 'Hesse' (Hessen) is generally held by scholars to derive from the ethnonym Chatti. For later military thought, this war is a rare specimen of a war with no record — neither side left a report, and a whole frontier has to be reconstructed from a single sentence in an ethnographic work. It is a reminder that most ancient wars were not ended by a set-piece battle but by endurance and by the depth of the country.
result: 結果沒有勝負可講，因為這場戰爭到塔西佗動筆時仍在進行。塔西佗寫下的不是「誰贏了」，而是攻守在兩族之間反覆易手：查蒂人向東壓，赫蒙杜里人向西頂，兩邊都沒有能力把對方徹底摧毀，也都沒有條件停手。這種僵持本身就是結果：它保住了易北河上游一段不落在任何一個強權手裡的走廊，同時把兩族都推上羅馬的視線。往後數十年，局勢由另一種力量決定——羅馬的界牆與軍鎮從萊茵與陶努斯向易北河上游推進，圖密善與圖拉真時代的戰役結束了查蒂人的獨立戰爭地位，赫蒙杜里人則成為羅馬在易北河上的正式盟邦，公元四世紀的晚期古代文獻中還能看到「赫蒙杜里人聚落」的名目，公元六世紀喬達尼斯把汪達爾人的古名指回「赫蒙杜里」。所以這場戰爭最終決定的不是兩族的勝負，而是中歐的權力版圖：它把原本沒有名字的森林與河谷變成羅馬前線的一部分，也讓兩個族名，一個留在黑森的地名裡，一個留在易北河畔的碑銘與聚落名裡。
resultEn: There is no score to report, because the war was still going on when Tacitus took up his pen. What he wrote was not 'who won' but the way attack and defence changed hands again and again between the two peoples: the Chatti pressed east, the Hermunduri pushed west, and neither could destroy the other, and neither had the conditions to stop. That stalemate was itself the result: it kept a stretch of the upper Elbe out of the hands of any single power, and at the same time brought both peoples into Rome's sight. In the decades that followed, the situation was settled by a different force — the limes and the forts advanced from the Rhine and the Taunus toward the upper Elbe, and the campaigns of the Domitian and Trajan era ended the Chatti's independent position in war, while the Hermunduri became formal clients of Rome on the Elbe; the name of a 'settlement of the Hermunduri' is still visible in the late-antique records of the fourth century, and in AD 551 Jordanes pointed the ancient name of the Vandals back to 'Hermunduri'. So what this war finally decided was not which of the two peoples won, but the political map of central Europe: it turned a country of forests and river valleys without a name into part of the Roman frontier, and left one ethnonym in the place-names of Hesse and the other in the inscriptions and settlement names of the Elbe.
